frontMatter.alt: Extraordinary Evangelism: Equipping You to Reach Your World for Christ. A Student Guide.
“But you shall receive power when the Holy Spirit has come upon you, and you will be my witnesses in Jerusalem and in all Judea and Samaria, and to the end of the earth.” Acts 1:8 ESV

blocks.html: We are incredibly grateful that you have decided to take the next step in your preparation to share the gospel with others. There is nothing more important than sharing the life-changing message of Jesus Christ. Years ago, I took a training class on evangelism and it changed my life and witness for Christ from that time forward.

The purpose of this Student Guide is to highlight some of the principles and truths found in the book, Extraordinary Evangelism which is a leader’s guide to this Student Guide. My prayer is that this Student Guide will equip you to confidently share the gospel with others. Let us boldly share the gospel so that we can by God’s grace turn others “… from darkness to light and from the power of Satan to God, that they may receive forgiveness of sins” (Acts 26:18).
May the Lord help you in this grand adventure to share the only news that will turn a person’s default destination from Hell to Heaven for all eternity!

blocks.html: We’re 14 of the Gospel.
Romans 1:16 (ESV) says, “For I am not ashamed of the gospel, for it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes, to the Jew first and also to the Greek.”
The gospel is the only news that can change a person’s default destination from 15.
Question: How has the Gospel impacted your own life?
The gospel contains both Good news and Bad news.
Romans 3:10 – “None is righteous, no, not one.”
James 2:10 – “For whoever keeps the whole law but fails in one point has become guilty of all of it.”
Matthew 5:48 – God desires that we reflect His character.
“You therefore must be perfect, as your heavenly Father is perfect.”
John 3:16 is the most famous verse in the Bible.
“For God so loved the world, that he gave his only Son, that whoever believes in him should not perish but have eternal life.”
God offers us amazing grace!
An acronym for grace is = 16
Pastor John MacArthur said the greatest verse in the Bible on the gospel is 2 Corinthians 5:21 which says,
“He made Him who knew no sin to be sin on our behalf, so that we might become the righteousness of God in Him.”

We deserve judgment. We deserve hell. But Jesus in His infinite love and mercy paid our sins’ debt by dying on the cross in our place. Our sin and guilt were charged to Christ and through faith in Christ’s atoning sacrifice, Christ’s righteousness is credited to us. Now we can stand before God sinless, just as Jesus is sinless.
Why is it important to share the “bad news” of the gospel?
Answer: Most people think that they are a pretty good person.
A 2003 Barna survey showed that most Americans do not expect to experience hell first-hand, and just half of 1 percent expect to go to hell upon their death.
Repentance and Faith are key requirements for true saving faith- Acts 3:19; Mark 1:15.
What is repentance? Repentance involves turning from your sin and turning to God in faith for forgiveness with a sincere desire to follow the Lord.

blocks.text: A SIMPLE WAY TO SHARE THE GOSPEL

blocks.html: The book, Extraordinary Evangelism, presents several effective ways to share the Gospel. One simple and powerful approach is rooted in John 3:16.
John 3:16 has been dubbed “the Hope Diamond of the Bible.” It’s the Gospel in miniature. Every believer should know this verse.
“For God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son that whoever believes in Him shall not perish but have eternal life.”
You can go to jesusonline.com/app and download their free JOApp that has this gospel tract and others also.
Here’s four simple points when sharing the gospel using John 3:16.

blocks.alt: Cover of John 3:16, the most amazing promise in the Bible

blocks.html: Have you ever felt like no one cares about you or you are unworthy of being loved?
Good News! God loves you infinitely no matter who you are. No person will ever love you more than God loves you!
“God is love.” I John 4:8
Human love from imperfect beings will often fail you but God’s love is forever. “I have loved you with an everlasting love.” Jeremiah 31:3 NIV
Just as the Universe is unfathomable, so God’s love for you is unfathomable!
The greatness of God’s love is seen in the greatness of the sacrifice that He gave …
The holy, almighty Creator of the Universe was willing to leave His throne room in Heaven and die a horrific death on the cross in our place for your sins and mine. John 10:18; Luke 9:22
“But God demonstrates his own love for us in this: While we were still sinners, Christ died for us.” Romans 5:8
Jesus said, “Greater love has no one than this, than to lay down one’s life for his friends” John 15:13,NKJV.

The Great Exchange – As Jesus was dying on the Cross, he said: “It is finished” (τετέλεσται) meaning “paid in full.” Jesus paid in full our sin debt on the cross. Christ’s righteousness is credited to us. Now we can stand before God sinless, just as Jesus is sinless.
Author Randy Alcorn wrote: “God … so much wants us not to go to hell that he paid a horrible price on the cross so that we wouldn’t have to.”

What do you need to believe in order to have a right relationship with God and receive eternal life? Jesus said, “I am the Way, the Truth and the Life: no one comes to the Father but through Me.” John 14:6.

blocks.text: Here are the “A,B,C”s of True Faith

blocks.html: Admit. Do you believe that you have sinned before God and need His forgiveness. “For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” Romans 3:23

Believe. Do you believe that Jesus Christ is God and rose from the dead? “If you confess with your mouth that ‘Jesus is Lord,’ and believe in your heart that God raised him from the dead, you will be saved.” Romans 10:9, John 11:25-26
Choose. Are you ready by faith to receive Christ and to follow Him. “But to all who did receive Him, who believed in his name, He gave the right to become children of God.” John 1:12

blocks.text: Admit + Believe + Choose = Become a child of God
(“Shall not perish but have eternal life”)

blocks.text: Great News – HEAVEN is a FREE GIFT

blocks.html: Heaven is not something we earn, but an incredible gift we are offered. “For it is by grace you have been saved, through faith—and this is not from yourselves, it is the gift of God—not by works, so that no one can boast” Eph. 2:8–9, NIV.
“The wages of sin is death, but the free gift of God is eternal life in Jesus Christ our Lord.” Romans 6:23
Will you choose to accept God’s amazing offer of forgiveness and eternal life? If you have never invited Jesus into your life, you can simply pray the following words.

“Dear Lord Jesus, thank you for dying for all my sins—past, present, and future. Thank you for giving me eternal life, which you made possible by your death and resurrection. I receive you as my Savior by faith, and desire you to be Lord of my life. Make me into the kind of person you want me to be.” I pray this in Jesus name, Amen!
If this prayer expresses the desire of your heart, I invite you pray this prayer right now.

blocks.html: “The Bible says in John 3:16, “For God so loved the world that He gave His one and only Son, that whoever believes in Him will not perish but have eternal life.”

That means God loves you so much that He sent Jesus to take the punishment for your sins by dying on the cross. If you believe and trust in Him, you’re forgiven and given eternal life with God – not because of what you’ve done, but because of what Jesus did for you.”
You might say: “God loves you so much that He sent Jesus to die for your sins, and if you trust in Him, you’ll have eternal life.”
Look for an opportunity to share John 3:16 this week with someone

Most of the following are abbreviated answers from Extraordinary Evangelism by Dave Chapman.
1. I’m an atheist; I don’t believe in God. Answer: Acronym: CAUSE.

C-CAUSE: Everything that exists has a cause. If you can’t believe that nothing caused something, then you don’t have enough faith to be an atheist. A-ACCURACY: The Universe is highly complex in its design. U-UNIVERSAL MORALITY: There must be a God to account for the sense of right and wrong. S-SUBJECTIVE EXPERIENCE: “Share your own story of how Jesus changed your life. Jeremiah 29:11 says, If you seek God, you will find Him.” E-EMPTY TOMB: Proves that Jesus is God. John 11:25-26. Jesus GRAVE is still EMPTY today!
2. What about those who have never heard?

God is perfectly just and merciful. Many people worldwide are coming to Christ through dreams and visions. Have them read: Philippians 2:9-11. Ask: What does this say to you? When you die, God is not going to ask you: “What about those who have never heard?” He is going to ask you: “What have you done with my Son’s offer of forgiveness? Would you like to invite Jesus into your life and heart today?”
3. Did Jesus Rise from the Dead?

Christ’s tomb is empty. No other great religious leader every claimed that he would rise from the dead except Jesus. The vast majority of secular and religious scholars state that Jesus died by crucifixion on Friday and rose from the dead on Sunday as predicted. John 11:25-26; Psalms 16:9-10. His Tomb is Empty!
4. Why Do People Suffer?
If there is no God, where did we get the standard of goodness by which we judge evil? God could decree by midnight all evil cease, but by 12:01 AM, none of us would be left.
5. Isn’t the Christian Experience only a Psychological Crutch?
The ultimate answer to the argument of wish fulfillment or that Christianity is a psychological crutch is based on irrefutable, objective facts of the resurrection of Christ from the dead.
6. How Do You Know the Bible is God’s Word?

items: • Internal Evidence: The Bible claims Divine Inspiration – 2 Tim. 3:16-17; 2 Pet. 1:21. Unity: 1,500 year; 40 authors, 3 continents – all say basically the same thing.
• External Evidence: Archaeology confirms countless details.
• Scientifically Accurate: The Bible is scientifically accurate.
• Fulfilled Prophecies: Up to 1,000 prophecies have been fulfilled.
• Experiential Evidence: The Bible has transformed millions of lives throughout history.

blocks.html: 7. Won’t a Good Moral Life Get Me to Heaven?
Every person has broken God’s moral law and the 10 commandments. Have the person read: James 2:10; Matthew 5:48; Romans 3:10,23.

Ask: What do these verses say to you? Say: “I want you to know that I too have broken God’s moral law, but I found forgiveness through Jesus. Would you like to receive the forgiveness that Jesus alone offers?”
8. Why Would a Loving God send someone to Hell?
Read: 2 Peter 3:9 where God desires all to come to repentance.

C.S. Lewis said, ““There are only two kinds of people in the end: those who say to God, ‘Thy will be done,’ and those to whom God says, in the end, ‘Thy will be done.’ All that are in Hell, choose it.”
9. The Bible is full or errors and there are so many translations.
Thousands of ancient manuscripts confirm its accuracy and reliability of the Bible.
Ask your friend: “Would you show me an error?” If they have a question about the Bible, recommend the website: “Gotquestions.org
10. What about other religions?

All religions of the world are based upon trying to be good; one word – “DO” but no one is perfect and they offer no assurance of salvation. Christianity is based on the word “DONE” (our sins were paid in full at the Cross). Jesus said, “I am the way, the truth and the life; no one comes to the Father but through Me” (John 14:6).
11. I’m Not Ready
Ask: “What would it take for you to be ready to receive Christ as your Savior and Lord?
12. There are too many hypocrites in the church?

Agreed, but if you were to join a perfect church, it wouldn’t be perfect anymore. Romans 3:23 says, “For all have sinned and fall short of the glory of God.” The only people who will get to heaven are forgiven people. Ask: “Would you like to receive the Lord’s offer of love and forgiveness?”
13. I’m a good person!

Ask: “Have you ever lived a perfect life?” Read them: James 2:10; Rom. 3:10; 23; Matt. 5:48; Isaiah 64:6. None of us are good enough to qualify for heaven. It would be like trying to swim to Hawaii. We’d all fall short no matter how good of a swimmer we may be.
14. I tried that, but it didn’t work for me.
Ask: What did you “try”? Review the gospel and share the story of the prodigal son – that God is there for them to return to Him (Luke 15).
15. I’m having too much fun.

Ask: According to what I’ve just shared with you (or what the Bible says), where will you go when you die? If they say “hell”, ask: Are you ready to accept Jesus Christ as your Savior? If their answer is “no”, you could say, “have a nice day!” – or say, “I’ll pray for you!”
16. God can’t forgive me.

Ask the person to read Romans 10:13 and reference the Thief on the Cross. Say: “If God can for forgive a murderer like the thief on the cross and the apostle Paul who killed Christians, He can forgive you.”
17. I’m a Gay person and associated with LBGQ community.” How should you
1. Start with Love as every person is created in the image of God (Genesis 1:27) and
everyone needs Christ equally (Romans 3:23). Jesus met people where they were at before addressing their sin (John 4:1-26, the Samaritan woman).
2. Listen & ask: “How did you come to understand your identity this way?”
3. Share your own story and the Gospel. Emphasize what Christ has done in your life –
forgiveness, peace, hope, transformation, heaven as a free gift (2 Cor. 5:17).
Jesus offers the same to them if they surrender their life to Christ.
4. Pray and Trust the Holy Spirit. The Holy Spirit convicts hearts (John 16:8). Pray for the
Lord to soften their heart to the Gospel. Emphasize God’s invitation (Matthew 11:28) to come to Christ.
5. Offer for them to come to a home bible study or to your church.

blocks.html: “We use God’s mighty weapons, not worldly weapons to knock down the strongholds of human reasoning and to destroy false arguments” (2 Corinthians 10:4 NLT).

Imagine you committed just 4 sins a day. Just 4 sins in thought, word or deed and even things that you should have done but didn’t do them (James 4:17). That would be over 1,000 sins on your record before a Holy God and if you lived to be 70 years of age, you would have more than 100,000 entries in God’s record book of your life. The consequence of sin is eternal separation from God. Place this record book with your name on it on your left hand. God loved us so much that He made a commitment to deal with all of our sins. The Bible says in Isaiah 53:6 (paraphrased): “We are all like sheep that have wandered away; each of us has decided to do our own thing. But God laid all of our sins and wrongs on Jesus. Put the record book of our sins on your right hand (on Jesus) to show that “God laid all our sins and wrongs on Jesus.” But when Jesus died on the cross, He took all your sins and wrote across your record: “Paid in Full.” Now your book is clean—your sins are forgiven, and your name will be written in the Book of Life if you ask Jesus to forgive you.
The A, B, C’s of Salvation (The main ideas start with the letter A, B. and C.
A is to accept Jesus as your Lord and Savior. When we accept Jesus, we agree to do our best to follow His ways as revealed in the Bible.
B is to believe what the Bible says about Jesus – who He is and what He did for us.
C is to confess the wrong things you have done, ask Him to forgive you and choose to follow Him.
The Chasm of Sin Illustration (or “Bridge Illustration”) shows the separation between God and man because of sin.

items: On one side is God, holy and perfect.
On the other side is man, sinful and separated from God.
Between them is a deep chasm of sin and death that no human effort—good works, religion, or morality—can cross.
Jesus Christ’s death on the cross forms the bridge across the chasm, allowing anyone who trusts in Him to come to God and receive eternal life.

Jesus – Our Substitute (from Y-Jesus.com)

Imagine entering a courtroom and you are guilty of murder. As you approach the bench, you realize that the judge is your father. Knowing that he loves you, you immediately begin to plead, “Dad, just let me go!”

With tears in his eyes he responds, “I love you, son, but I’m a judge. I can’t simply let you go.” Presenting the evidence against you, he bangs the gavel down and declares you guilty. Justice cannot be compromised, at least not by a judge. But because he loves you, he steps down from the bench, takes off the robe, and offers to pay the penalty for you. And in fact, he takes your place in the electric chair.

This is the picture painted by the New Testament. God stepped down into human history, in the person of Jesus Christ, and was crucified on the cross for us. Jesus is not a third-party whipping boy being punished for our sins, but rather he is God himself. Stated more bluntly, God had two choices: to punish us for our sin, or to receive the punishment himself. In Christ, he decided to pay the penalty for us.

In other words, God’s perfect justice is completely satisfied by the death of his Son, Jesus Christ. All of our sins—no matter how bad they are or have been—are completely paid for by the blood of Christ. Paul writes,

“…yet now he has brought you back as his friends. He has done this through his death on the cross in his own human body. As a result, he has brought you into the very presence of God, and you are holy and blameless as you stand before him without a single fault.” —Colossians 1:22, NLT

Your personal testimony is one of the greatest tools you have when you share the gospel. People like stories, especially ones that are true. Stories emotionalize information. Jesus often told stories (parables). No persuasive argument will ever be a substitute.
Examples:

items: Gerasene demoniac – Mark 5
Blind man healed by Jesus – John 9
Woman at the well – John 4
Paul the Apostle – Acts 22; 26
